# Konecta Color System & Theme Management Skill

## Overview

This project implements the Konecta brand color palette with a complete light/dark theme system using CSS variables and signals-based state management.

## Konecta Color Palette

### Official Brand Colors

```typescript
// Primary Brand Colors
Konecta Blue:      #2A01CD  (primary-500)
Konecta Dark Blue: #0F0F72  (primary-900)
Konecta Blue2:     #A6B7FF  (konecta.blue2, used in dark mode)
Konecta Yellow:    #F0FA00  (warning-500)

// Neutrals
Konecta White:     #FFFFFF  (surface-0)
Konecta Light:     #F2F3F7  (surface-50)
Konecta Dark:      #262626  (surface-900)
Konecta Black:     #0F0F0F  (surface-950)

// System Colors
System Green:      #0E9F6E  (success-500)
System Red:        #F05252  (danger-500)
System Red Dark:   #9B1C1C  (danger-800)

// Additional
Success Story:     #DF622B  (konecta.successStory)
```

### Color Scale Extension

Each base color has a full 50-950 scale for nuanced usage:

```typescript
primary: {
  50:  '#f0f0ff',  // Lightest tint
  100: '#e0e0ff',
  200: '#c7c1ff',
  300: '#a89cff',
  400: '#7d6aff',
  500: '#2A01CD',  // Base color (Konecta Blue)
  600: '#2400ad',
  700: '#1e008e',
  800: '#170072',
  900: '#0F0F72',  // Konecta Dark Blue
  950: '#0a0050',  // Darkest shade
}
```

## Theme System Architecture

### Single Source of Truth: colors.constants.ts

**All color values are defined in `src/app/core/constants/colors.constants.ts`**

```typescript
// src/app/core/constants/colors.constants.ts
export const COLORS = {
  primary: { 500: '#2A01CD' }, // Konecta Blue
  surface: {
    0: '#ffffff', // White
    50: '#F2F3F7', // Light gray
    900: '#262626', // Dark gray
    950: '#0F0F0F', // Near black
  },
  success: { 500: '#0E9F6E' }, // Green
  danger: { 500: '#F05252' }, // Red
  warning: { 500: '#F0FA00' }, // Yellow
  info: { 500: '#3b82f6' }, // Blue
} as const;
```

### Architecture Flow

```
colors.constants.ts (TypeScript - Single Source of Truth)
    ↓ imported by
    ├── tailwind.config.ts
    │       ↓ exposes via theme('colors')
    │       tailwind-css-variables.mjs (Tailwind plugin)
    │           ↓ generates at build time
    │           CSS variables (--p-*, --p-button-*, --p-card-*, etc.)
    │               ↓ used by
    │               PrimeNG components (Button, Card, InputText, Tree)
    │       ↓ also generates
    │       Tailwind CSS classes (bg-primary-500, text-surface-900, etc.)
    │
    └── theme-colors.service.ts
            ↓ provides
            Reactive signals for TypeScript/ECharts (this.colors.textColor())
```

**Current Status:**

- ✅ 4 componentes configurados: Button, Card, InputText, Tree
- ⚠️ 111 componentes pendientes (ver `.github/UI/PRIMENG-COMPONENTS-STATUS.md`)

### Workflow to Edit Colors

**1. Edit the single source:**

```typescript
// src/app/core/constants/colors.constants.ts
export const COLORS = {
  primary: { 500: '#2A01CD' }, // Change this value
  // ...
} as const;
```

**2. Rebuild the application:**

```bash
pnpm start  # or pnpm build
```

**3. Everything updates automatically:**

- ✅ Tailwind classes (imported via tailwind.config.ts)
- ✅ ThemeColorsService signals (imported in service)
- ✅ CSS Variables (generated by tailwind-css-variables.mjs plugin)
- ✅ PrimeNG components (use generated CSS variables)

### 1. Define Colors (colors.constants.ts)

**This file contains color VALUES. Edit colors here ONLY.**

```typescript
// src/app/core/constants/colors.constants.ts
export const COLORS = {
  primary: {
    500: '#2A01CD', // Konecta Blue
  },
  surface: {
    0: '#ffffff', // White
    50: '#F2F3F7', // Light gray
    900: '#262626', // Dark gray
    950: '#0F0F0F', // Near black
  },
  // ...more colors
} as const;
```

### 2. Import Colors (tailwind.config.ts)

### 2. Import Colors (tailwind.config.ts)

**This file imports colors and generates CSS classes automatically.**

```typescript
// tailwind.config.ts
import { COLORS } from './src/app/core/constants/colors.constants';

export default {
  content: ['./src/**/*.{html,ts}'],
  darkMode: 'class', // CRITICAL: Use 'class', NOT ['class', 'dark']
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        // All color scales imported directly from constants
        primary: COLORS.primary,
        surface: COLORS.surface,
        success: COLORS.success,
        danger: COLORS.danger,
        warning: COLORS.warning,
        info: COLORS.info,
        gray: COLORS.gray,
      },
    },
  },
  plugins: [],
};
```

### 3. CSS Variables Generated Automatically (Plugin)

**Plugin: `tailwind-css-variables.mjs` (root of project)**

⚠️ **CSS variables are generated during Tailwind build** - No file to edit

**To regenerate after editing colors:**

```bash
pnpm start   # Development with watch
pnpm build   # Production build
```

The Tailwind plugin reads colors via `theme('colors')` and generates all PrimeNG CSS variables automatically during build.

**Light Mode (`:root`)**

```css
:root {
  /* Primary colors */
  --p-primary-50: #f0f0ff;
  --p-primary-100: #e0e0ff;
  --p-primary-500: #2a01cd; /* Konecta Blue (from COLORS.primary[500]) */
  --p-primary-900: #0f0f72; /* Konecta Dark Blue */
  --p-primary-contrast: #ffffff;

  /* Surface colors */
  --p-surface-0: #ffffff; /* Konecta White (from COLORS.surface[0]) */
  --p-surface-50: #f2f3f7; /* Konecta Light (from COLORS.surface[50]) */
  --p-surface-900: #262626; /* Konecta Dark (from COLORS.surface[900]) */
  --p-surface-950: #0f0f0f; /* Konecta Black (from COLORS.surface[950]) */

  /* Text colors */
  --p-text-color: #262626; /* Dark text on light bg */
  --p-text-hover-color: #0f0f0f;
  --p-text-muted-color: #757575;

  /* Component-specific */
  --p-card-background: #ffffff;
  --p-card-border-color: #e0e0e0;
  --p-card-color: #262626;

  --p-button-primary-background: #2a01cd;
  --p-button-primary-color: #ffffff;
  /* ... all other component variables */
}
```

**Dark Mode (`:root.dark`)**

```css
:root.dark {
  /* Primary colors - lighter for contrast */
  --p-primary-500: #a6b7ff; /* Konecta Blue2 */
  --p-primary-contrast: #0f0f0f;

  /* Surface colors - inverted */
  --p-surface-0: #0f0f0f; /* Konecta Black (was White) */
  --p-surface-50: #262626; /* Konecta Dark (was Light) */
  --p-surface-900: #f2f3f7; /* Konecta Light (was Dark) */
  --p-surface-950: #ffffff; /* White (was Black) */

  /* Text colors - light for readability */
  --p-text-color: #f2f3f7; /* Light text on dark bg */
  --p-text-hover-color: #ffffff;
  --p-text-muted-color: #bdbdbd;

  /* Component-specific */
  --p-card-background: #262626;
  --p-card-border-color: #424242;
  --p-card-color: #f2f3f7;

  --p-button-primary-background: #a6b7ff;
  --p-button-primary-color: #0f0f0f;
  /* ... all other component variables */
}
```

**Why CSS Variables?**

- PrimeNG Aura theme expects specific variable names
- Component-specific variables (--p-card-_, --p-button-_) needed for proper styling
- Script ensures consistency between TypeScript constants and CSS
- Automatic dark mode mapping

### 4. Apply in Styles (src/styles.css)

```css
/* Import PrimeNG theme configuration FIRST */
@import './styles/primeng-theme.css';

/* Tailwind directives */
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;

@layer base {
  /* Native color-scheme support */
  :root {
    color-scheme: light;
  }

  :root.dark {
    color-scheme: dark;
  }

  /* Prevent flickering during theme toggle */
  .theme-transitioning,
  .theme-transitioning * {
    transition: none !important;
  }

  /* Body defaults - uses CSS variables */
  body {
    font-family:
      -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif;
    background-color: var(--p-surface-0); /* #ffffff in light, #0F0F0F in dark */
    color: var(--p-text-color); /* #262626 in light, #F2F3F7 in dark */
    transition:
      background-color 200ms ease-in-out,
      color 200ms ease-in-out;
  }

  /* Ensure text inherits color from body */
  h1,
  h2,
  h3,
  h4,
  h5,
  h6,
  p,
  span,
  div,
  li {
    color: inherit;
  }

  /* Smooth transitions for PrimeNG components */
  .p-card,
  .p-button,
  .p-inputtext {
    transition:
      background-color 200ms ease-in-out,
      border-color 200ms ease-in-out,
      color 200ms ease-in-out;
  }

  /* Force correct colors on PrimeNG elements */
  .p-card .p-card-title,
  .p-card .p-card-content {
    color: var(--p-text-color);
  }
}
```

### 5. Manage with ThemeService (Signals-Based)

```typescript
import { Injectable, signal, effect, inject, PLATFORM_ID } from '@angular/core';
import { isPlatformBrowser } from '@angular/common';

@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root',
})
export class ThemeService {
  private platformId = inject(PLATFORM_ID);

  readonly isDarkMode = signal(false);

  constructor() {
    if (isPlatformBrowser(this.platformId)) {
      // Load saved preference or use system preference
      const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem('theme');
      const prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;

      this.isDarkMode.set(savedTheme === 'dark' || (!savedTheme && prefersDark));

      // Apply theme reactively
      effect(() => {
        this.applyTheme(this.isDarkMode());
      });
    }
  }

  toggleTheme(): void {
    this.isDarkMode.update((v) => !v);
  }

  private applyTheme(isDark: boolean): void {
    if (isPlatformBrowser(this.platformId)) {
      const html = document.documentElement;

      // Disable transitions temporarily
      html.classList.add('theme-transitioning');

      // Toggle dark class
      html.classList.toggle('dark', isDark);

      // Set native color-scheme
      html.style.colorScheme = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light';

      // Persist to localStorage
      localStorage.setItem('theme', isDark ? 'dark' : 'light');

      // Force reflow to ensure synchronous style application
      void html.offsetHeight;

      // Re-enable transitions after theme applied
      setTimeout(() => {
        html.classList.remove('theme-transitioning');
      }, 50);
    }
  }
}
```

### 5. Theme Toggle Component

```typescript
import { Component, inject, ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core';
import { ButtonModule } from 'primeng/button';
import { ThemeService } from '../../../core/services/theme.service';
import { LucideAngularModule, Sun, Moon } from 'lucide-angular';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-theme-toggle',
  imports: [ButtonModule, LucideAngularModule],
  template: `
    <button
      pButton
      (click)="themeService.toggleTheme()"
      [rounded]="true"
      [outlined]="true"
      [attr.aria-label]="
        themeService.isDarkMode() ? 'Switch to light theme' : 'Switch to dark theme'
      "
      class="flex items-center gap-2"
    >
      <lucide-icon [img]="themeService.isDarkMode() ? Sun : Moon" [size]="16" />
      <span>{{ themeService.isDarkMode() ? 'Light' : 'Dark' }}</span>
    </button>
  `,
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
})
export class ThemeToggleComponent {
  readonly themeService = inject(ThemeService);

  protected readonly Sun = Sun;
  protected readonly Moon = Moon;
}
```

## Color Usage Patterns

### Text Color - Use Inheritance

**DO NOT** explicitly set text colors:

```html
<!-- ❌ WRONG -->
<h1 class="text-surface-900 dark:text-surface-100">Title</h1>
<p class="text-surface-700 dark:text-surface-200">Text</p>

<!-- ✅ CORRECT -->
<h1>Title</h1>
<p class="opacity-80">Secondary text</p>
```

**Why?** Text inherits from `body { color: var(--p-text-color) }` which automatically adapts to theme.

### Background Colors - Use CSS Variables

```html
<!-- ✅ Use CSS variables for dynamic theming -->
<div style="background-color: var(--p-surface-50)">Content</div>

<!-- ✅ Use Tailwind classes with theme awareness -->
<div class="bg-surface-50 dark:bg-surface-900">Content</div>
```

### Icons - Use Semantic Colors

```html
<!-- ✅ Icons should have explicit semantic colors -->
<lucide-icon [img]="CheckCircle" class="text-success-500 dark:text-success-300" />
<lucide-icon [img]="XCircle" class="text-danger-500 dark:text-danger-300" />
<lucide-icon [img]="AlertTriangle" class="text-warning-600 dark:text-warning-400" />
```

## PrimeNG Component Theming

PrimeNG components automatically use CSS variables:

```html
<!-- Primary button uses --p-primary-500 -->
<p-button label="Save" severity="primary" />

<!-- Success button uses --p-green-500 -->
<p-button label="Confirm" severity="success" />

<!-- Danger button uses --p-red-500 -->
<p-button label="Delete" severity="danger" />

<!-- Card uses --p-surface-* for backgrounds and borders -->
<p-card>
  <p>Content automatically themed</p>
</p-card>
```

## Opacity Utility Classes

For secondary/muted text without hardcoded colors:

```html
<p>Primary text</p>
<p class="opacity-80">Secondary text (80%)</p>
<p class="opacity-70">Muted text (70%)</p>
<p class="opacity-60">Very muted text (60%)</p>
```

## Common Theme Patterns

### Card with Theme-Aware Content

```html
<p-card>
  <ng-template pTemplate="header">
    <div class="flex items-center gap-2 p-4">
      <lucide-icon [img]="Star" class="text-primary-600 dark:text-primary-300" [size]="24" />
      <h3 class="text-lg font-semibold">Card Title</h3>
    </div>
  </ng-template>

  <p>Card content inherits text color</p>
  <p class="opacity-80">Secondary information</p>
</p-card>
```

### Status Indicators

```typescript
@Component({
  template: `
    @if (status() === 'success') {
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
        <lucide-icon [img]="CheckCircle" class="text-success-500" />
        <span>Success</span>
      </div>
    }
    @if (status() === 'error') {
      <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
        <lucide-icon [img]="XCircle" class="text-danger-500" />
        <span>Error</span>
      </div>
    }
  `
})
```

## Debugging Theme Issues

### Verify CSS Variables

```javascript
// In browser console
const root = document.documentElement;
const style = getComputedStyle(root);

// Light mode
style.getPropertyValue('--p-text-color'); // Should be #262626
style.getPropertyValue('--p-surface-0'); // Should be #ffffff

// After toggling to dark mode
style.getPropertyValue('--p-text-color'); // Should be #F2F3F7
style.getPropertyValue('--p-surface-0'); // Should be #0F0F0F
```

### Verify Dark Class

```javascript
document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark'); // true in dark mode
```

### Verify localStorage

```javascript
localStorage.getItem('theme'); // 'light' or 'dark'
```

## Performance Considerations

### Build Time vs Runtime

- **CSS Variables**: Generated at **build time** (fast)
- **theme() calls**: Resolved at **runtime** (slow with 100+ calls)
- **Result**: ~3 second builds vs 60+ second builds

### Transition Strategy

- Disable transitions during programmatic toggle (`.theme-transitioning`)
- Only enable smooth transitions for user interactions
- Apply transitions to specific properties, not universal selectors

### Force Reflow

```typescript
void html.offsetHeight; // Forces browser to apply styles synchronously
```

## Adding New Colors

**1. Edit `src/app/core/constants/colors.constants.ts`:**

```typescript
export const COLORS = {
  // Existing colors...
  newColor: {
    50: '#...',
    500: '#HEX_CODE',
    900: '#...',
  },
} as const;
```

**2. Import in `tailwind.config.ts`:**

```typescript
colors: {
  // Existing imports...
  newColor: COLORS.newColor,
}
```

**3. Add variables in plugin (if using with PrimeNG):**

Edit `tailwind-css-variables.mjs` to add the new color variables for light and dark modes.

**4. Rebuild:**

```bash
pnpm start  # or pnpm build
```

**5. Use in code:**

```html
<div class="bg-newColor-500">Content</div>
<div style="background: var(--p-new-color-500)">Content</div>
```

## Best Practices Summary

1. ✅ **Single source of truth**: All colors in `colors.constants.ts`
2. ✅ **Automated plugin**: Tailwind plugin generates CSS variables at build time
3. ✅ **Inherit text colors**: No `text-*` classes on text elements
4. ✅ **Semantic icon colors**: Explicit colors for visual meaning
5. ✅ **Use CSS variables**: `var(--p-*)` for dynamic theming
6. ✅ **Opacity for hierarchy**: `opacity-80` for secondary text
7. ✅ **Prevent flickering**: `.theme-transitioning` during toggle
8. ✅ **Persist preference**: `localStorage` + system preference
9. ❌ **No hardcoded colors**: All colors from constants
10. ❌ **No manual CSS variables**: Plugin generates them automatically
